renderTool: tools/render-one-reconstruction.mjs with the shared GPU mutex

detail.method: Second actual 3D camera subfrustum render; not a crop or enlargement of the first output.

observedImprovements: Front karahafu ends no longer turn upward into a narrow pinched profile; the crown remains at the measured screen height.
The rear gable panel is 1.27 m farther behind the previous face, with four separately spaced structural timber ribs in front.
Lower side eaves and colonnade supports have actual raised geometry; the second pass restored the two-eave height separation.
The front slabs now have visible rounded arrises, real pitting, small crowns and independent settlement; PBR data is a CC0 granite face at 0.3173828125 m repeat.
Native subfrustum inspection caught inflated slabs and flag-like moss in the first candidate; the corrected source reduces the heights and replaces flags with closed low cushions.
remainingDifferences: The main hall still has simplified bracket and carving silhouettes, regular roof tile rows, and insufficient real wood variation compared with the photograph.
The front granite remains too uniform and warm in the current native daylight; the reference has stronger dark mica, pale mineral clusters, lichen and irregular erosion.
Rounded moss cushions are still visibly simplified in the enlarged native detail.
A source/reference axis offset and local roof-corner residual remain; screen landmark agreement does not establish photographic fidelity.
unchanged: Camera position, target and focal length
Sanctuary, Buddha, large lanterns, trees, water, and other buildings
scope: One bounded actual mesh/PBR correction and one render-driven revision, not a finished 10-scene film.
